title: The Filolial Boom
paragraphs: “No matter what that guy does, we’ll be able to fend him off. We just need to take him out the moment he shows up.”

“Even Gaelion doesn’t fully grasp just how threatening he can be when he gets serious. But even so, based on all the wild stuff that’s gone down in Ofumi’s world, I think we need to take precautions.”
“Um, Gaelion-chan, does this have anything to do with the Melromarc situation?”
“That’s right. If we introduce those Hakuko siblings to Trash, victory is guaranteed. It’ll really bring them down.”
Rival spoke as if he knew something I also knew, as if it were his own business. It’s not like I didn’t say anything on purpose! I just forgot! I swear!
“Why?”

“Because those siblings are the children of Trash’s younger sister. The younger sister, in particular, is in terrible shape from her illness, but apparently, if she’s treated with medicine, she looks exactly like Trash’s younger sister.”
“Huh!?”
“The Spear Hero… that’s a case Naofumi and the others warned us about before. We should at least secure them.”
“Did you forget our earlier conversation? We can’t make them our subordinates!”
It’s impossible because of the country’s circumstances. Seriously, Siltvelt is such a pain in the neck.
“If we use the excuse that she has a connection to the Panda Clan to save her, and then make her a subordinate of the Panda Clan, wouldn’t things work out as long as Naofumi doesn’t get involved?”
The representative of the Shusaku clan pondered Rival’s question for a moment.
“True… If it’s actually true that Hakuko is a relative of that Wise King of Wisdom, it wouldn’t be a completely impossible move… but it is dangerous in many ways. Is that information confirmed?”
It really is a difficult situation. We must consider the timing carefully.
“There’s no doubt about it. In fact, because of that incident, the Wise King of Wisdom has calmed down enough to put his hostility toward Naofumi aside.”

At this point, Rival recounted a story—apparently gathered in the first world—about the Tiger siblings’ parents. Stories like how, after that Trash sister went missing, she more or less eloped with a child who was apparently the leader of the Hakuko clan—and that’s how the Tiger siblings were born.
“If we treat her properly, we could use her as a trump card in negotiations. As a representative of your country, what do you think?”
Rival asked the representative of the Shusaku clan.

“…We should refrain from getting too close to the Shield Hero. If Larsazusa maintains only a personal relationship with him, we might be able to manage… It would also create a favor with Melromarc, and being able to keep that wise and prudent king in check would be a major advantage. Of course, we’ll need to exercise great caution.”
“It’s a problem when you go and decide things on your own, though.”

“Panda, if things stay as they are, those guys are in a tight spot. If the Spear Hero administers treatment now, it’ll solve any future problems. I don’t think it’s a bad deal for you—what do you say?”
Panda pauses briefly to consider Rival’s words. Well, buying Yggdrasil medicine over and over again is a burden, after all. Or maybe he’s simply doing the math.
“…Will it really work? I’ve heard that even Yggdrasil medicine doesn’t cure it.”
“I can say that with absolute certainty. I’ve heard from others exactly where he is, so there’s no mistake.”
“…Well, if this means I won’t have to shell out any more money on this, I’ve got no complaints. That said, I still think taking care of this is just a hassle.”
“By the way, I also know where the guy your grandfather wants to meet is. To be honest, it’s creepy how perfectly Gaelion fits the description—it’s almost unsettling.”
Panda furrows his brows at Rival’s words.
“Since we’re at it, you should help recruit him.”
“What are you thinking, introducing him to Grandpa’s arch-enemy? Are they going to start killing each other or something?”
“Of course, it’s to get him to owe me a favor for the future and to do my part as a dutiful grandson. If they don’t get along, we can even aim for them to take each other down.”
“No, seriously, is that really a good idea? Shouldn’t we just try talking to him, at least?”
While Father scolded Rival, the panda fell even deeper into thought. Heh heh heh… Rival has finally started to slip up. Let him be disappointed by Father just like this.
“Lars-chan?”
Do you really hate that old panda’s training that much?
“By the way, I hear even the Spear Hero learned the basics from him.”
“It’s all thanks to my own hard work!”
I practically learned how to read the room from Father and the others! In the end, I just listened to what he had to say to a certain extent.
“He’s not a bad guy, so I think he’ll at least listen to what you have to say. What do you say?”
“…Fine. Do whatever you want.”
“Huh? Is that really okay!?”
“Pandaaaaaaa! Are you backing out now!?”
“Well, it doesn’t seem like I’d lose anything even if I fail. And I’d really appreciate it if you’d stop calling me a panda.”
Panda has shifted the subject. What we’re talking about now is a completely different matter from that topic.

“…Honestly, thanks to Lord Gaelion being here, I can take various precautions in advance—figuring out things I couldn’t understand from Lord Kitamura’s explanation and finding solutions—so it’s a huge help.”
“That’s true…”
“Yes.”
For some reason, everyone present—including Father—nodded in unison at Éclair’s words. Éclair, what exactly do you mean by that? I take exception to that implication that I’m incompetent.
“I’m doing my very best to explain things!”
“Yeah. I know that. I’m always grateful. It’s just that Motoyasu-kun isn’t very articulate and tends to forget things easily, so Gaelion-chan is simply filling in the gaps for him.”
Father spoke in a very gentle tone, as if trying to reason with me. But that’s unnecessary consideration! Right now, that kindness just makes me even more frustrated. Grrr… You rival!
“If Naofumi—who possesses the skill to enhance the effectiveness of medicine—or the Spear Hero administers it, both of them should recover.”
“Yggdrasil potions are expensive, though… Do you think you could arrange for that? Or would we have to gather the ingredients and make them ourselves?”

“I can certainly arrange that. It’s a bit pricey, but I suppose it can’t be helped. Above all, setting aside issues between races and speaking purely from a personal standpoint, I want to help as well.”
The Shusaku guaranteed it.
“Then I’ll leave it to you. I’ll treat it as an investment in the future… and I’ll do my best, too.”
“Thanks to you heroes, Siltvelt’s financial and food supply issues have improved, so please don’t worry about it.”
“That’s a relief.”
“So, I’ll go treat the person who’s Lars-chan’s grandfather’s arch-enemy, and Motoyasu, can you take care of the Hakuko siblings?”
“Of course! I, Motoyasu, will definitely rescue the Tiger siblings!”

If it’s Father’s order, I have no choice but to obey. I’m not happy about being sent to mediate with a Rival, but there’s nothing I can do about it. So, even though I was extremely reluctant, I set out on a business trip to the monster merchant’s shop in Zeltoble, where the Tiger Siblings were based.
I handed the monster merchant in Zeltoble a letter of introduction from Rival and another from the monster merchant in Siltvelt.
“Well, well… the Spear Hero. I’ve heard that our nephew was treated quite favorably by you in Melromarc. Thank you for coming. Yes.”
This is the monster merchant that Father used to do business with in the previous loop. In this loop… ah, that’s right—I bought up all of Filolial-sama’s eggs from the monster merchant in Siltvelt.
“Thank you for your continued support.”
“And… oh my, this must be Lord Larsazusa, the fighter known by the famous epithet ‘Bamboo Grove.’ Zeltoble has become rather quiet lately.”
“Are there any interesting characters around?”
“With the Queen of Earthquakes gone, Zeltoble isn’t very exciting these days. I think things will liven up again with Larsazusa’s return. Yes.”

It seems Panda is, after all, somewhat famous even in Zeltoble. I could make a big splash if I wore the Filolial Mask, but since I’m busy with my Idol activities right now, I’ll just keep it in mind as a way to make some money down the line.
“That said, though… I’ve got the work I’m doing right now, so I can’t exactly go around groveling… I’d do it if I got permission, but even then, it’s a question of whether it’d actually be any fun.”

Apparently, Panda has raised her level and stats quite a bit alongside Father and Rival. Since she hadn’t mastered Ki yet, she was getting taken down by Old Man Panda’s techniques, but I’m sure she’ll be able to handle that level of challenge in no time. If a fighter like her were to enter the Colosseum, I think she’d rake in a fortune, don’t you? After all, she’s basically undefeated.
“The fighter making a name for herself lately is the one called Nadia. I’d say it’s only a matter of time before she gets a nickname.”

Oh? Ren seems to still be in hiding, as usual. He’s not an Itsuki or anything—how long does he plan to stay hidden away in Zeltoble? I’d guess he’s just wasting his time leveling up deep in the mountains of Zeltoble. It’s about time for the revival of Cal Mira Island, so he might show his face eventually. Ren’s ability to lie low is probably limited to that extent.
“Huh… I’m looking forward to the day we can fight each other.”
“By the way, this Nadia. Apparently, she’s quite the heavy drinker, and she’s become popular in Zeltoble for that reason as well. Yes.”
“A heavy drinker, huh. Someone who can beat me… Well, the world’s a big place, so I suppose there must be someone out there.”

After the panda fell silent for a moment, she corrected herself. That must be Father! Oh? For some reason, Big Sister’s older sister flashes through my mind, but I’m pretty sure her name is different… It must just be my imagination!
“So, what brings you to our establishment this time?”
“There should be a pair of Hakuko siblings staying here.”
“I’ve got a little business with them. You must have some idea where their money’s coming from, don’t you?”
“Ah, I see.”
“Just because you’re asking doesn’t mean we’ll back down if you try to reel us in, you know?”
The panda, who looks a lot like Father, is threatening the monster merchant in some way.
“If you pull any funny business, who knows what that famous Spear Hero might do.”

……This negotiation style is just like Father’s from the first world. It seems safe to say there’s a common negotiation style in this area. After all, Father from the first world also seemed to be more of a tough guy when it came to rough stuff.
“Oh, how terrifying. Do you really think we’d pull a stunt like that against the famous Larsazusa and the Spear Hero?”
Of course I think they would. Father from the first world used to say, “Those guys will do anything for money.”
“I don’t know about that. The fact that you’ve made a name for yourselves in Zeltoble makes you seem suspicious, too.”
“Then I’ll take that to mean it depends on our future relationship. Yes, sir.”
“Also, are you selling Filolial-sama?”
“The Spear Hero… You still want one, even though there are already so many of them?”
“Of course. Not only have I been saving up little by little lately, but thanks to Yuki-chan and the others’ hard work, our profits have gone up.”

Come to think of it, we haven’t been getting much from the thieves lately. Thieves are a resource, you know. Dragons are resources too! As for the Shieldfreeden issue, wouldn’t hunting dragons solve it? I’ll talk to Father about it next time. But more importantly, it’s about Filolial-sama.
“I plan to keep expanding the lineup. By regularly introducing new faces, Filolial-sama’s popularity will skyrocket.”
Our goal is to create that large-scale idol group Father was talking about.

“I’m terribly sorry, but due to the Spear Hero and Shield Hero promoting Filolial primarily in Shieldfreeden and spreading the word across the region, demand has skyrocketed, and we’re constantly running out of stock. So it’s difficult to provide them right away. Yes.”
“Wow… it’s a Filolial-sama boom, isn’t it! Well, I suppose that can’t be helped!”
Even if I can’t buy them here, I should head to the Filolial-sama producers I haven’t been able to meet during this run. They’re sure to have them for sale there.
“Are you sure? There’s a chance they’re just using nice-sounding words to cover up the fact that they won’t sell to the Spear Hero, you know?”
“Ah, that’s certainly possible. Why won’t they sell Filolial-sama to us?”
“Isn’t it because you messed something up in Melromarc?”
What on earth is Panda talking about? I just bought up all of Filolial-sama’s eggs from the monster merchant in Melromarc.
“Absolutely not!”
The monster merchant in Zeltoble replied, sweat pouring down his face like a waterfall. Does that mean he’s lying?
“I take pride in my business. While I do enjoy deceiving customers with lies, I detest misrepresenting the goods I sell. Yes!”
“I know it’s a bit odd for me to say this, but isn’t that a bit much…? They’re still a bunch of people I just don’t get.”
“So, does that mean Filolial-sama really is sold out?”
“I’ve heard that the Spear Hero spares no expense when it comes to Filolial-sama. I deeply regret that we weren’t able to prepare for this. Yes.”
“Well, looks like it’s true, then.”
It seems the Panda has taken the monster merchant’s words—spoken with a look of frustration—at face value. It appears there’s no mistake here.
“I suppose there’s nothing we can do about it.”
“To begin with, Spear Hero, are you even allowed to increase the number of Filolials without the Shield Hero’s permission? Aren’t you just going to end up making him roll his eyes again?”
